title: Reward Codes make staking activity attributable to a specific frontend, Integrator and Prime Agent
content:
A.2.2.11.1.4.2 allocates each Prime Agent "a share of the Core Governance Reward proportional to the SKY staked through eligible frontends maintained by the Integrators it manages." A.2.2.11.1.4.2.1 supplies the mechanism: staking amounts are "tracked using Reward Codes," which eligible frontends "pass... identifying the Integrator and associated Prime Agent when users stake SKY." Each code is assigned by Operational GovOps and "recorded in the associated Instance of the Core Governance Reward Primitive in the Agent Artifact."

The problem being solved is that a stake transaction says nothing about which interface produced it. Without attribution, a reward for frontend provision cannot be paid proportionally to actual usage — only as a flat grant, which pays a neglected frontend the same as a well-run one.

The registration path is what makes the code trustworthy. Codes are issued by Operational GovOps, not self-declared, and recorded in the Prime's Artifact, so attribution is governed data rather than a frontend's assertion about itself. Combined with the compliance gate in A.2.2.11.1.2, only a frontend that has been admitted can earn.

The generalisable pattern: pay for a public good by making the private contribution *measurable* at the point of use, then tie eligibility to a registry. The exposure is that whoever holds the code controls the measurement — codes embedded in client-side interfaces are trivially copyable, so the integrity of the split depends on eligibility enforcement rather than on the code itself.
description: Eligible frontends pass a unique code when users stake SKY, assigned by Operational GovOps and recorded in the Prime's Artifact, converting an unattributable on-chain action into a measurable
